papers.title: Investigating the Surface Characteristics of Complex Geometrical Features on Ti-6Al-4V Alloy Processed through WEDM
papers.abstract: Abstract The present study focuses on producing an interface at micro- and nano-level on complex curved and plane features of Ti-6Al-4V (α + β) alloy through wire electric discharge machining (WEDM) which simultaneously does machining and surface modification. The process parameters such as servo voltage, pulse on-time, pulse off-time and wire speed are used as input controls to comprehend the surface attributes of complex curved features at different scales. A thorough statistical, parametric, surface integrity, modified layer, layer hardening, surface porosity and surface spectroscopical analyses are carried out for a comprehensive evaluation of surface properties. Multi-attribute optimization resulted in optimized process settings S V (70 V), P off (40 μs), P on (8 μs) and W S (6 mm/s) achieving 75.51% combined desirability of both responses. The predicted and experimental results are validated under a 95% confidence interval showing less than 5% error. The optimized parametric conditions show 3.58 μm surface roughness on curved features and 3.27 μm on plane features.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究了Ti-6Al-4V合金线切割加工后的表面特性，但未涉及增材制造或疲劳/力学性能，与用户关注的后处理对AM材料力学性能的影响关联较弱。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not evaluate fatigue or mechanical performance of Ti-6Al-4V, nor does it address post-processing of additively manufactured material; it only studies surface characteristics of WEDM on conventionally processed Ti-6Al-4V.

summary_en.motivation: This study investigates surface characteristics of complex geometrical features on Ti-6Al-4V alloy processed by WEDM.
summary_en.method: Statistical, parametric, surface integrity, and spectroscopic analyses were performed to optimize WEDM parameters.
summary_en.result: Optimized parameters achieved surface roughness of 3.58 μm on curved features and 3.27 μm on plane features.
summary_en.validation: Predicted results were validated experimentally with less than 5% error under a 95% confidence interval.
